description:
Cancel an order this session created, or a paid order from another conversation, while RendReal still allows it.

Irreversible — the order and any artwork work on it are gone. An order is
cancelled whole: there is no per-item cancel, so when the customer names one
product of an order with several items, tell them the cancel ends every item
in it. Call it as soon
as the customer asks to cancel: an unpaid order is cancelled on that call when
Compass reads their `customer_words` as a request to cancel it. Any other call,
such as for a paid order or on words that ask for something else, takes two
calls: the first fails with `OrderCancelConfirmationRequiredError` and sends
nothing. Then quote the
order's `reference_id` back to the customer and wait for a clear yes. Only after
they agree, call again with `confirmed=true` and the brief cancellation
question plus their exact answer in `customer_words`. `confirmed=true` on a
call Compass has not refused yet, or with no new customer words since the
refusal, is refused the same way.
`customer_words` is an exact quote of only the customer's request to cancel
this order on the first call. On the confirming call, include only the brief
cancellation question and the customer's exact answer, even if they repeat
the same words, such as "yes". Exclude the rest of their message and all
conversation history. Never paraphrase. Never cancel on a hint, and never pick
the order yourself when the session has several — ask.

For an order this session created, pass its `order_id`. For an order from
another conversation, pass instead the `reference_id` and `email` the customer
gives you — the order reference and the email it was paid with, exactly as typed,
never guessed — on both calls. `ForeignOrderNotFoundError` means the pair matched
no order: ask them to re-check both. Only a paid order from another conversation
can be cancelled here: `ForeignOrderNotPaidError` means it is unpaid; give the
customer its reason as written. A foreign `order_id` alone fails with
`OrderNotInSessionError` and no upstream call. RendReal decides
what is cancellable: an unpaid order, or a paid order in the short window
after payment, before production starts. A refusal (`OrderNotCancellableError`)
means production has started and no retry will help: tell the customer and
offer customer support. After a confirmed cancel, read `refund`: for
`refunded`, tell the customer the payment is refunded to the card they paid
with; for `requested`, give them `refund_note` as written; for `none`, say
nothing about a refund. Promise no timing for a refund,
and never tell the customer they were not charged.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED. `status` is the order's live status
after the cancel, read back from RendReal: only `CANCELLED` there means it
is cancelled. `already_cancelled: true` means it was cancelled before this
call and nothing was sent. `OrderCancelNotConfirmedError` means RendReal
accepted the request but the order has not changed state yet — say the
request went through but is unconfirmed, and re-check with `order_get` on
the customer's next message. `OrderCancelOutcomeUnknownError` means the
request reached RendReal but its outcome could not be confirmed: say neither that
it is cancelled nor that nothing changed; say you could not confirm it, and
check `order_get` on their next message; for an order from another conversation,
re-check with `order_lookup` instead. After a confirmed cancel the cart line the
order came from is orderable again.

customer_words.description: Exact customer cancellation request on the first call. On the confirming call, include only the brief cancellation question and the customer's exact answer. Exclude unrelated message text and conversation history.

name: order_cancel

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Cancel an order
